subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should allowlisted shell-shaped commands auto-execute only when OpenClaw can build an enforceable command plan, or should current plan-miss approval behavior be treated as the supported security boundary and documented?
rationale: This changes when a command bypasses explicit approval; automation cannot safely choose between restoring documented convenience and preserving the stricter shell enforcement boundary without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin matches
options.body: Repair the macOS path so enforceable allowlist matches such as safe tilde expansion or fully planned chains run without prompts, while plan-miss cases still require explicit approval.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed approval behavior and update docs plus warning text to explain command-shape limits on Darwin.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell commands
options.body: Run matched Darwin commands even when no enforced command can be materialized, accepting a larger shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin matches
recommendation.body: Repair the macOS path so enforceable allowlist matches such as safe tilde expansion or fully planned chains run without prompts, while plan-miss cases still require explicit approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The current gate, warning text, and most recent exec approval history in this path point to vincentkoc.
